diagnosis.hypothesis: Initial validation showed only guest1<->web1 failed while other paths were healthy. Reads confirmed guest1 had the correct 10.10.20.10/24 address and default route via leaf1, and leaf1 guest gateway 10.10.20.1/24 was present and enabled. On leaf2, I found an active static host route 10.10.20.10/32 pointing to a blackhole next-hop-group, which specifically broke traffic toward guest1. I deleted that route on leaf2. Final public success validation passed, with all lab connectivity checks succeeding including guest1<->web1.
diagnosis.reference: On leaf2, a more specific static route to 10.10.20.10/32 (guest1) is configured as a blackhole (discard), so traffic to guest1 is dropped.

arguments.reason: Public validation shows only guest1<->web1 fails, while guest1 has correct address/default route and leaf1 guest gateway is up. Leaf2 has an active static host route 10.10.20.10/32 to blackhole, which specifically breaks return traffic from web1 toward guest1 without affecting other paths.

action.reason: Public validation shows only guest1<->web1 fails, while guest1 has correct address/default route and leaf1 guest gateway is up. Leaf2 has an active static host route 10.10.20.10/32 to blackhole, which specifically breaks return traffic from web1 toward guest1 without affecting other paths.
